entries.feature: Follow selected process is an explicit semantic setting: a standard checkbox Toggle (node 68, label Follow selected process, shortcut Shift-Command-F) and a status Text (node 69) in a Row (node 67) between the column chooser and the table, off in the creating commit, disabled with an explanation in the uncollected shell; its one handler is the toggle's VALUE_CHANGED, whose boolean turns follow on for the inspector's resolved process or off, and which always publishes the value the server holds so a refused request unchecks the client's box

entries.feature: Sticky follow over CPU resorting: while on, the table's keep_visible hint (PX-017-G01) names the followed item ID, set once at turn-on and once per retarget and never again for a sample, sort or filter, so the generic client reveals the item wherever a commit moves it; follow never promotes; the followed row keeps its item ID and no row is created; the status names the PID, name and row

entries.feature: Non-follow mode never hints or promotes on a sample or a selection: no keep_visible is held, ordinary selection preservation is the client's, anchored to item IDs, and a resort moves neither the viewport nor the selection off its process

Stops honestly: when the followed process ends follow turns itself off, its hint is cleared and the status says so, and a new process that reuses its PID (a new item ID) is never followed, selected or revealed, in the same sample or later; a filter or the row limit that hides it stops follow with that reason; a selection that names no shown row stops it too; follow never moves to another row by itself
